$comment: Open-gaps register (plan J-7). Reviewed, curated entries; the generator appends entries derived from the matrix (untested mechanisms, per-polarity gaps, unsupported cells). Every entry needs an owner ("unassigned" when none is named) and a status: open | in-progress | accepted-limitation.

gaps.title: ML-DSA hedged signing with a caller-supplied rnd is not reachable through PKCS #11
gaps.detail: CK_SIGN_ADDITIONAL_CONTEXT carries hedgeVariant and context only; there is no parameter for an explicit rnd, so NIST hedged sigGen expected signatures cannot be reproduced on either engine. Shown in the workbench as an explicit skip (mldsa-skip-hedged-rnd-*) and here as unsupported rows.

gaps.title: HashML-DSA with SHA2-512/224 or SHA2-512/256 has no PKCS #11 mechanism
gaps.detail: PKCS #11 v3.2 §6.67.7 defines no CKM_HASH_ML_DSA_<hash> for these two hashes; the NIST sigVer groups for them are listed as notExecuted in mldsa_sigver_test.json.

gaps.title: ML-DSA internal interface (raw M′) is not expressible through PKCS #11
gaps.detail: No PKCS #11 v3.2 mechanism exposes Sign_internal/Verify_internal on a caller-supplied M′; the NIST internal-interface groups without external mu are listed as notExecuted.

gaps.title: KMAC256 vector case quarantined
gaps.detail: kmac_test.json tg0/tc0: the expected MAC does not match the cited NIST KMAC Sample #4 (63 bytes for a 512-bit macLen). Quarantined in the manifest; it cannot count as evidence, so CKM_KMAC_256 has no registered test.

gaps.title: 106 C++/Rust C_GetMechanismInfo disagreements
gaps.detail: The two engines list the same 165 shared mechanisms but report different key-size ranges and/or CKF_ flags for 106 of them (mechanism-inventory.generated.json crossEngine.sameTypeDifferentInfo). Treated as findings, not verdicts; cells one engine does not advertise are unsupported for that engine.

gaps.title: 7 mechanisms advertised by Rust only
gaps.detail: CKM_RIPEMD160, CKM_RIPEMD160_HMAC, CKM_RIPEMD160_HMAC_GENERAL, CKM_PQCTODAY_FRODOKEM_KEY_PAIR_GEN, CKM_PQCTODAY_FRODOKEM_ENCAPSULATE, CKM_KECCAK_256 and CKM_EC_MONTGOMERY_KEY_DERIVE are listed by the Rust engine only; their C++ cells are unsupported.

gaps.title: Rust dispatches CKM_HPKE / CKM_HPKE_KEM_KEY_PAIR_GEN without advertising them
gaps.detail: The dispatch report (mechanism-dispatch-report.generated.json) finds 0x80000013/0x80000014 on Rust dispatch paths but not in C_GetMechanismList, so they are outside every denominator here. Also dispatched-not-advertised: Rust CKM_BIP32_*_LEGACY and C++ CKM_RIPEMD160*.

gaps.title: Native targets not run
gaps.detail: macOS, Linux x86-64 and Linux Arm64 native builds have not executed these registered tests; the native artifact column is "not run" and never counts as pass.

gaps.title: Hardware targets not run
gaps.detail: i.MX 95 and KV260 have not executed these registered tests; no frozen evidence bundle exists. The hardware artifact column is "not run" and never counts as pass.

gaps.title: Run results recorded only for the workbench and katRunner, on the wasm engines, in Node
gaps.detail: src/data/validation/run-results/ holds one recorded run of useAcvpSuite (all categories, both engines) and one of every registered katRunner case (both engines asserted, the Rust engine recorded — the engine the KAT surfaces use), executed in Node against the shipped .wasm bytes. The mechanism probes and the conformance cases have no recorded results, so their cells are never reported as passed. A browser-host run and a signed evidence bundle (H-1, H-7) do not exist yet.

gaps.title: Native 976/815-check engine suites not in the evidence pipeline
gaps.detail: The larger native C++/Rust conformance suites are not imported, so none of their cases appear in this matrix.

gaps.title: PKCS #11 API-behavior matrix not built
gaps.detail: OASIS Tier A cases and the generated Tier B profile-condition probes that exercise sessions, login, objects and attributes are registered (testRegistry oasis.api-only, profile.api-only) but are outside this algorithm × operation matrix.

gaps.title: SLH-DSA NIST sigGen cases registered but not executed
gaps.detail: slhdsa_ctx_test.json /sigGen cases are in the manifest for identity but no runner executes them (deterministic sigGen byte-match), so SLH-DSA sign has round-trip evidence only.

gaps.title: Supported ACVP test types (AFT/MCT/LDT/VAL) not declared per algorithm
gaps.detail: The capability map declares parameter sets, variants and boundaries, but not which ACVP test types each capability should support; the matrix lists only the test types its registered NIST cases exercise.

gaps.title: Some test surfaces are not in the test registry
gaps.detail: Not registered: Learn-module demos outside KatValidationPanel (the SUCI flow's own step-by-step tool among them) and the *.local.test.ts engine suites that are not run-results recorders. Their evidence does not appear in this matrix. (The katRunner suci-profile-b chain is registered since 2026-09-24: steps 3-7 against TS 33.501 Annex C.4.4.1.)

gaps.title: Rust engine accepts all 6 invalid NIST ML-KEM encapsulation/decapsulation keys
gaps.detail: The NIST ACVP ML-KEM encapDecap VAL key-check cases (mlkem_encapdecap_val_test: modified H, ek values too large) are accepted by the Rust engine: its C_EncapsulateKey / C_DecapsulateKey paths perform no FIPS 203 §7.2 encapsulation-key or §7.3 decapsulation-key input checks (bundle 417c47a2; unchanged on pqctoday-hsm origin/main). The workbench rows stay failing on Rust (acvp.07b.keycheck). Engine defect — not patched in the hub.

gaps.title: C++ HashSLH-DSA wraps M′ twice — valid NIST pre-hash signatures rejected
gaps.detail: OSSLSLHDSA.cpp (bundle 7795799b, lines ~341-402) builds M′ = 0x01 ‖ len(ctx) ‖ ctx ‖ OID ‖ PH(M) itself and then passes it to OpenSSL's pure SLH-DSA via EVP_DigestSign together with OSSL_SIGNATURE_PARAM_CONTEXT_STRING, so OpenSSL wraps it again as a pure message: all 5 valid NIST pre-hash sigVer signatures are rejected and deterministic pre-hash signatures differ at byte 0. Unchanged on pqctoday-hsm origin/main. Rows stay failing on C++ (acvp.09c). Engine defect — not patched in the hub.

gaps.title: ML-KEM wrong-length inputs: return codes differ from PKCS #11 v3.2 and between engines
gaps.detail: Wrong-length ciphertext at C_DecapsulateKey: Rust returns CKR_ENCRYPTED_DATA_INVALID (not in the return-value list of PKCS #11 v3.2 §5.18.9), C++ returns CKR_WRAPPED_KEY_LEN_RANGE. The C++ engine accepts a decapsulation key 1 byte short at C_CreateObject; both engines accept a short encapsulation key. The boundary rows (acvp.07b.boundary) pin each engine's observed code, so a pass there means 'behaves as pinned', not 'conforms'.

gaps.title: PBKDF2 iteration floor differs between engines (Rust refuses c < 1000)
gaps.detail: The Rust engine refuses CKM_PKCS5_PBKD2 with iterations < 1000 (rust/src/ffi.rs:11125 at 417c47a2: CKR_ARGUMENTS_BAD, a code that does not name the parameter); the C++ engine accepts c = 1 (SoftHSM_keygen.cpp ~3012-3030 at 7795799b). A policy divergence, not an algorithm error. The c = 1 oracle cases (pbkdf2_test tests/0) are therefore not registered; katRunner and the workbench run the c = 4096 cases, which pass on both engines.

gaps.title: ECDSA P-521 NIST sample failed on C++ — hub CKA_EC_POINT encoding (fixed hub-side)
gaps.detail: Root cause (triage 2026-09-24): hsm_importECPublicKey wrote the DER OCTET STRING length of the 133-byte P-521 point as the single byte 0x85, which DER reads as '5 length octets follow'; the C++ engine parsed a garbage CKA_EC_POINT and rejected the NIST ACVP-Server ECDSA-SigVer-FIPS186-5 sample (workbench §33), while Rust passed because it reads the raw CKA_VALUE copy. Hub adapter bug, not an engine defect. Fixed by the X.690 long-form length (softhsm/helpers derOctetString); the re-recorded run shows the case passing on both engines. Kept on record until the release freeze re-captures evidence on the browser host.

gaps.title: SUCI key-injection helper is rejected by the C++ engine
gaps.detail: hsm_injectTestKey unwraps the raw EC scalar with C_UnwrapKeyAuthenticated using a template that carries CKA_EC_PARAMS; the C++ engine rejects it with CKR_ATTRIBUTE_READ_ONLY (the same unwrap without CKA_EC_PARAMS succeeds). katRunner suci-profile-b steps 1-2 (import only, not registered) therefore error on C++; steps 3-7 import with C_CreateObject and pass on both engines. The KAT surfaces run the Rust engine. Hub helper limitation.
